description: A lightweight VS Code extension that wraps the arduino-cli gRPC daemon (ArduinoCoreService) — compile, upload, and monitor without leaving the editor.

config.monitorAutoReconnect: Reopen the serial monitor automatically after an upload.

config.eagerDaemonStart: Start the arduino-cli daemon as soon as a project containing a sketch.yaml is opened, so profile mode resolves immediately. When off, the daemon starts lazily on the first command.

config.debugAdapter: Debug adapter to use: "auto" detects an installed adapter; or set "cortex-debug", "cppdbg", any adapter type, or "custom" to use the full template below.
config.debugAdapterConfig: Fields merged into the generated debug configuration (override any field). When the adapter is "custom", this is the entire launch template; supports ${executable}, ${toolchainPath}, ${toolchainPrefix}, ${gdbPath}, ${server}, ${serverPath}, ${svdFile}, ${programmer}.
config.debugInterpreter: GDB command interpreter to use (e.g. "mi", "mi2"). Leave empty for the default.
debug.fqbn: Override the board FQBN for this debug session.
debug.programmer: Override the programmer for this debug session.
debug.snippetDescription: Debug an Arduino sketch on a connected board
config.boardManagerUrls: Additional Board Manager URLs (e.g. for ESP32, STM32).
config.alwaysExportBinaries: Always export compiled binaries alongside the sketch.
config.unsafeLibraryInstall: Allow installing libraries from untrusted sources (ZIP/Git).
config.verbose: Enable verbose output for compile, upload, and bootloader operations.
config.updateNotifications: Check for arduino-cli updates on startup.

walkthrough.title: Get Started with Arduino Sketch Studio
walkthrough.description: Compile, upload, and monitor Arduino sketches in plain VS Code.
walkthrough.installCli.title: Install the Arduino CLI
walkthrough.installCli.description:
This extension drives the official **arduino-cli** — install it once and you're set.

- **macOS:** `brew install arduino-cli`
- **Windows:** `winget install ArduinoSA.CLI`
- **Linux / manual:** [installation guide](https://arduino.github.io/arduino-cli/latest/installation/)

Then confirm it's wired up: [Show Daemon Version](command:arduinoCli.showVersion).
walkthrough.openSketch.title: Open or create a sketch
walkthrough.openSketch.description:
Open a folder that contains an `.ino` file, or scaffold a fresh one.

[New Sketch](command:arduinoCli.newSketch)
walkthrough.selectBoard.title: Select your board
walkthrough.selectBoard.description:
Tell the extension which board you're targeting. If its core isn't installed yet, it offers to install it for you.

[Select Board](command:arduinoCli.selectBoard)
walkthrough.compileUpload.title: Compile & upload
walkthrough.compileUpload.description:
Open your `.ino` and use the buttons in the top-right of the editor: **Compile** (✓) and **Upload** (⬆).

[Compile now](command:arduinoCli.compile)
walkthrough.monitor.title: Watch your board talk back
walkthrough.monitor.description:
Read what your board prints over serial, or graph live numbers with the plotter.

[Open Serial Monitor](command:arduinoCli.openMonitor) · [Open Serial Plotter](command:arduinoCli.openPlotter)
walkthrough.manage.title: Manage cores & libraries
walkthrough.manage.description:
Open the **Arduino** view in the Activity Bar (the circuit-board icon) to install, update, or remove platforms and libraries — no commands to memorize.

[Open the Arduino view](command:workbench.view.extension.arduinoCli)
walkthrough.blockly.title: Optional: program with blocks
walkthrough.blockly.description:
Prefer dragging blocks to typing C++? Install the sister extension **Blocks Editor** — a visual, Scratch-like editor that generates real Arduino code and builds & uploads through this extension.

[Install Blocks Editor](command:extension.open?%5B%22linucs.blocks-editor%22%5D)

It's completely optional — this extension works fully on its own.
